title: The Influence Toolkit
gist: QCon London talk by BBC senior architect Henry Wilson using the BBC Sounds re-architecture (40+ microservices, Scala/Thrift to Node.js and serverless AWS, monolithic team split into platform and experience teams) to argue influence is the key senior-IC skill, offering a toolkit: vision selling, context docs, a support/resistance matrix focused on active resistors, RFCs plus ADRs, parity-first tradeoffs, Slack presence, allies and radical candor.

themes.theme: Influence as the core senior-IC skill

insights.claim: Henry Wilson, a BBC senior architect, argues that for senior individual contributors and senior engineering managers in large organisations, influence is the single skill that contributes most to effectiveness.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: In large engineering orgs, technical strategy execution depends on soft-power capabilities, not just technical talent.
insights.quote: the single skill which contributes most to your effectiveness in your role is influence
insights.locator: I want to start today with a thought exercise

insights.claim: Wilson says senior ICs, unlike managers, cannot rely on positional authority and must build influence through relationships, usefulness and measured interventions, which then acts as a catalyst at key decision inflection points.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Explains why staff-plus/architect roles succeed or fail on relationship capital.
insights.locator: Influence for these roles is not the same

insights.claim: Wilson contrasts the isolated 'ivory tower architect' handing down context-free designs with the 'friendly neighborhood architect' teams want to work with, and says the difference is entirely communication and influence.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Architecture functions separate from engineering (as at the BBC) risk ineffectiveness unless they embed with teams.
insights.quote: The architect in the ivory tower handing down their perfect designs, but devoid of context
insights.locator: Finally, I want to talk about influence

insights.claim: Wilson argues that in large organisations senior ICs spend far more time communicating than writing code, and that code and design documents are themselves forms of communication.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Productivity tooling for senior engineers should target communication workflows, not only coding.
insights.locator: Another reason that I want to talk about influence

themes.theme: BBC Sounds re-architecture: scale and complexity

insights.claim: BBC Sounds serves 4.8 million weekly active users, and the BBC's RSS platform delivers 85 million content downloads a month on third-party platforms like Apple and Spotify.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Quantifies the BBC's audio distribution scale and its dependence on third-party platforms.
insights.locator: I'm a senior architect responsible for the teams

insights.claim: The BBC began a large-scale BBC Sounds re-architecture about a year ago as part of moving to the product operating model and platform engineering, because it needs to evolve its digital offering to stay relevant.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Large public-media orgs adopting platform engineering signals the model's mainstream diffusion.
insights.locator: BBC Sounds Re-Architecture

insights.claim: Under the new structure the catalog team moves to platform, the former business-led team splits into a platform API half and an experiences half, with platform owning core metadata APIs (podcasts, radio programmes, audiobooks, live stations) and experiences owning personalisation and features like international mode.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Illustrates a concrete platform/experience split pattern for content businesses.
insights.locator: With the move to platform engineering

insights.claim: The BBC Sounds backend comprised over 40 microservices with uneven documentation, some mixing user-activity personalisation into core API responses, because the original design prioritised performance over decoupling.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Typical legacy microservice sprawl; decoupling is a prerequisite for cross-product features.
insights.locator: Project Complexities

insights.claim: Inter-service communication relied on Thrift RPC built with Finatra and Finagle, which are no longer actively maintained, and leadership wanted to move off Scala due to recruitment, retention and knowledge-sharing issues.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Signals declining enterprise appetite for the Scala/Twitter-stack ecosystem in favour of more mainstream stacks.
insights.locator: Persuading teams to revisit design decisions

insights.claim: Three engineering teams of 20-plus engineers had operated as one monolithic team for over 5 years, previous split attempts had been resisted, and a single on-call rota covered all services.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Socio-organisational inertia is often the binding constraint on re-architecture timelines.
insights.quote: People problems are almost always harder than technical problems.
insights.locator: The project also had social complexities

themes.theme: Selling the vision and handling resistance

insights.claim: Wilson sold the change on faster delivery—arguing smaller teams with manageable estates have less fear and more confidence to evolve software—and on unlocking cross-experience features like recommending 'The Traitors: Uncloaked' podcast to iPlayer viewers, which is currently impossible.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Platform engineering at the BBC aims to break silos for cross-product recommendations, a monetisation/engagement lever for media firms.
insights.locator: First Steps

insights.claim: Wilson set the expectation that the change was not optional because senior leadership had set a clear strategy, noting this creates tension for IC roles that depend on positive relationships.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Top-down strategy still needs IC-level relationship management to execute without morale damage.
insights.locator: I also needed to set expectation

insights.claim: Wilson uses spoken communication for rapport but scales influence beyond one-to-ones with context documentation co-written with key engineers covering problem, challenges, rationale and next steps.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Written context docs are a scalable influence mechanism for large teams.
insights.quote: Spoken communication is valuable but it doesn't always scale.
insights.locator: It's absolutely essential to communicate the vision

insights.claim: Wilson rebutted pushback that a proper re-architecture would take three years by saying the BBC lacks the luxury of 3-year re-architecture projects that deliver no audience-facing value.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Incremental, value-delivering migrations beat big-bang rewrites in budget-constrained orgs.
insights.quote: We don't have the luxury of indulging in 3-year re-architecture projects which don't deliver audience-facing value.
insights.locator: Inevitably, during this vision setting period

insights.claim: Wilson's support/resistance matrix divides people into active supporters, passive supporters, passive resistors and active resistors, and says most influence effort should go to active resistors, who are often a disproportionately small number.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Change programmes should concentrate effort on a small set of active resistors for outsized results.
insights.quote: The active resistors are the group that you should spend most of your time trying to influence
insights.locator: When we're thinking about pushback

insights.claim: Wilson notes active resistance can be covert—people saying nothing while quietly continuing work that doesn't align with strategy—and that long-tenured team members can wield outsized influence regardless of title.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Hidden resistance from tenured staff is a key execution risk in reorganisations.
insights.locator: Down in the bottom right

themes.theme: Decision mechanics: RFCs, ADRs and accepted tradeoffs

insights.claim: Wilson broke the re-architecture into decision areas—ways of working, AWS account management (all infrastructure had been in a single set of accounts), service ownership, an InnerSource model for common libraries, contract testing across the platform/experience boundary, and splitting core services.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Shows the concrete governance workstreams a platform-engineering split requires.
insights.locator: Breaking Down the Problem

insights.claim: Wilson drove consensus by leading an RFC per significant problem area, widening input from a tight group once consensus formed, then recording outcomes tersely in ADRs, citing Michael Nygard's blog post, backed by regular stakeholder check-ins.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: RFC+ADR is a repeatable decision-making pattern for large engineering estates.
insights.locator: Lastly, thinking about how to split functionality

insights.claim: The platform team first built an API on a parity basis mirroring the existing core service rather than redesigning it, accepting more platform/experience coupling for a while because redesigning while splitting would cause unacceptable delays.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Parity-first migration trades architectural purity for speed and autonomous teams.
insights.quote: Attempting to redesign the API while also splitting the technical estate would have been too complicated
insights.locator: A big part of selling this vision

insights.claim: Wilson accepted a transitional operational-support approach, as out-of-hours rotas and BAU maintenance could not immediately match new team structures without risking operational stability.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Operational continuity constrains how fast org restructures can actually land.
insights.locator: I consider this an acceptable tradeoff

themes.theme: Hands-on technical steering: stack and scope

insights.claim: The platform API team chose Node.js over Scala, and Wilson steered them to reuse a monorepo approach with CDK for infrastructure and CI/CD that he had built in sister teams, sharing code samples and running targeted knowledge sessions.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Data point on enterprise migration from Scala to Node.js and AWS CDK-based monorepos.
insights.locator: Zooming In: Platform Tech Stack

insights.claim: Wilson pushed a serverless-first, most-managed-option approach using Lambda and ECS Fargate to escape the maintenance burden of EC2, falling back to serverful options only for compelling reasons.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Signals continued enterprise shift from EC2 toward managed/serverless AWS services.
insights.quote: taking a serverless-first approach and only falling back to serverful options where compelling reasons existed
insights.locator: I was also influential in guiding the team

insights.claim: Wilson uses presence in Slack team channels to spot decision points and share prior art, but stresses following up directly with key players.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Chat platforms are a key channel for senior-IC influence and knowledge reuse.
insights.locator: Slack is so rich

insights.claim: Wilson got senior leadership to cancel many sprints of planned work to remove Thrift from the program metadata service—meant to fix Finatra and Finagle security vulnerabilities—because it would be thrown away within a year when platform replacements arrived.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Shows how sequencing re-architecture can avoid wasted engineering spend on soon-to-be-retired systems.
insights.quote: That work would ultimately be thrown away in less than a year
insights.locator: Zooming In: Core Metadata Service

insights.claim: Wilson resisted engineers' desire for a larger reimagining of personalisation, pushing for simple, fast options over elegance to avoid scope creep blocking audience value.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Scope discipline is a key lever on re-architecture timelines.
insights.quote: Not a hack, but a pragmatic path forward.
insights.locator: Some of the engineers were keen

insights.claim: Wilson says allies are essential because even the best visions fail without support, and applies Kim Scott's 'Radical Candor'—caring personally while challenging directly—to influence.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Coalition-building determines whether technical strategies gain traction.
insights.quote: the best ideas and the strongest visions will still fail to gain traction if you don't have support, because change is hard
insights.locator: Some of the discussions around the core

insights.claim: Wilson reports the BBC Sounds re-architecture is not finished but on track: all major decision points agreed and documented in ADRs, platform APIs progressing and experience integration underway, though team morale has at times been lower than he would like.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Progress status of a major BBC platform migration, with morale as the acknowledged weak spot.
insights.quote: We're not finished, but we're on track.
insights.locator: Measuring Success

insights.claim: Wilson admits his vision selling fell short with some team members, says 100% buy-in is unrealistic for significant change, and endorses disagree and commit.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Leaders should plan for partial buy-in rather than consensus on major change.
insights.locator: Some of my personal approaches

insights.claim: Wilson proposes measuring influence on technical matters by the proportion of team decisions aligned with desired outcomes, and on social matters through clues like morale, fewer difficult conversations and active resistors moving to passive or supportive.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Gives a practical scorecard for assessing senior-IC effectiveness.
insights.locator: How do you measure success?

insights.claim: Wilson values indirect feedback from relationships: a platform API engineer told him the new team structure and tech stack let the team build much faster than before, which he treats as an anecdotal sign his approach worked.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Early anecdotal evidence that the platform split improved delivery speed.
insights.locator: If you have friendly, positive relationships

insights.claim: On choosing battles, Wilson argues senior ICs should sometimes let teams pursue a flawed approach to learn firsthand if the cost is a couple of weeks, but not if it would cost six months.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Cost-bounded learning heuristic for technical leadership interventions.
insights.quote: ok, we'll lose a couple of weeks, but they'll learn something really valuable, then maybe you let them do it
insights.locator: Often, people will learn more

insights.claim: Wilson says that if an organisation's strategy diverges too much from your views and you fail to influence it, you must disagree and commit or find another job.
insights.speaker: Henry Wilson
insights.so_what: Strategy misalignment at senior levels drives attrition of senior technical staff.
insights.locator: Henry Wilson: That's really hard
